item.title: BeOne Degradation vs Inhibition
item.description:
• Summary: BeOne is pursuing a targeted protein degradation approach rather than traditional inhibition for an oncology target. The company’s strategy aims to achieve more durable and potent effects by degrading disease-driving proteins, potentially overcoming resistance mechanisms seen with conventional inhibitors.
  • MoAs: N/A
  • Sources: ApexOnco

item.title: IDEAYA Exits Werner and Pol Theta
item.description:
• Summary: IDEAYA Biosciences has announced the discontinuation of its two early-stage programs targeting Werner helicase (WRN) and Pol Theta (polymerase theta). The decision reflects a strategic prioritization, likely focusing resources on more advanced pipeline candidates. Werner and Pol Theta are implicated in DNA repair mechanisms relevant to cancer.
  • MoAs: WRN helicase inhibitor (discontinued), Pol Theta inhibitor (discontinued)
  • Sources: ApexOnco

item.title: Exelixis Zanzalintinib Delay
item.description:
• Summary: Exelixis has reported a delay in the clinical development of zanzalintinib, its next-generation tyrosine kinase inhibitor. The setback may affect timelines for ongoing or planned trials in various solid tumors. Zanzalintinib is designed to inhibit multiple kinase targets involved in tumor growth and angiogenesis.
  • MoAs: Multi-targeted tyrosine kinase inhibitor (VEGFR, MET, etc.)
  • Sources: ApexOnco

item.title: Dark Proteins Cancer Immunotherapy
item.description:
• Summary: Researchers are exploring "dark proteins" as novel targets for cancer immunotherapy using advanced proteomics.
  • MoAs: Targeting uncharacterized proteins to elicit immune responses.
  • Sources: STAT News

item.title: Makary Defends Replimune Rejection
item.description:
• Summary: FDA official Dr. Makary defended the agency's rejection of Replimune's oncolytic virus therapy RP1 combined with nivolumab for melanoma, highlighting concerns over trial design and efficacy endpoints. The decision has heightened tensions between the FDA and biotech developers seeking accelerated approval for novel immunotherapies.
  • MoAs: RP1: engineered herpes simplex virus that selectively replicates in tumor cells, expresses GM-CSF and a fusogenic protein to stimulate antitumor immunity. Nivolumab: anti-PD-1 checkpoint inhibitor.
  • Sources: BioSpace
